O 101 Purpose and Statement of Intent

This employee handbook of personnel procedures is intended to be a general statement of the personnel procedures of the City and is.subject to change at any time without ptior notice to employees.

Title Chapter 7 of the Georgia Code creates employment at will conditions in the State of Georgia and all employees of the City are “at will” employees. This means that all employees are employed for an indefinite time period and that the employer and employes are each free to terminate the employment relationship at any time without notice for any reason.

The City Council is the appointing authority for the City, However, by Charter the Mayor is the Chief Executive Officer of the City, and therefore, is the only City official authorized to appoint and terminate (including accepting the resignation of) employees. Statements, contrary to these “at will” provisions, regarding conditions of employment, made by any other unauthorized City official or employee, should not be construed or interpreted by the employee as modifying or changing the conditions of employment contained in this handbook. All employees are “at will” employees and serve at the pleasure of the appointing authority.

Although the City is declaring itself as an “at will” employer, the City wants to ensure high morale for its employees and a high level of productivity for the people of the City. To accomplish these goals, officials feel that fair and equitable treatment of applicants and employees is desirable. Althongh all jobs are not identical and, therefore, all conditions of employment will hot be identical, many personnel practices can be the same in various departments. Among those practices are methods of requesting, earning and accumulating annual and sick leave. By including these provisions in the procedures, City officials hope to provide equitable treatment to employees and to assure good personnel practices. .

In no casé should any provision contained in this handbook be interpreted as an act of conveying the expectation of continued employment or any other relaxation of the doctrine of the City.

Neither should any provision contained in this handbook be interpreted as creating any subsidiary contractual obligation or privilege or condition of employment between the City and the employee except those specifically listed below.

1, An employee may earn, accumulate and take annual leave as specified by thesé procedures. 2. An employee may earn, accutnulate and take sick leave as specified by these procedures.

- 3. An employee may observe holidays as specified by these procedures.

4, Eligible employees may participate in a City-wide retirement program: only if one is available. Specific provisions for eligibility and participation may be as outlined in any retirement ordinance passed of amentied by the City Council, or by another entity, authority, administrator or provider.

- 5. Eligible employees may participate in group iaskrance and group medical coverage if offered by the City. Specific provisions for eligibility and
